newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo Nikkei to drift at 20,000 as market eyes yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo Nikkei to drift at 20,000 as market eyes yen.

text.p: Tokyo stocks will likely drift near the 20,000 threshold on a key index on Friday with investors looking for signs of more strength in the yen against the dollar, brokers said. They said bargain-hunting interest in domestic demand-reliant issues and laggards would continue.
On Thursday, the 225-share Nikkei average fell 153.41 points or 0.76 percent to close at 20,056.31. Nikkei June futures fell 180 points to 20,060.
"The 114-115 yen to the dollar level is the limit for exporters, and selling of such shares will emerge at that level," said Kazuhiro Igarashi of Mito Securities.
Overnight in London, the yen climbed briefly past 115 yen to the dollar.

Brokers said market participants were likely to avoid active trade in blue chips until the Federal Open Market Committee meeting next week, which could result in a credit tightening by the U.S. central bank.
